# Rutland Driveways & Landscaping

> Family-run driveway, landscaping and building company in Rutland, eight years trading. Vuba approved resin bound installer, NVQ qualified, five year written workmanship guarantee. Rutland Driveways & Landscaping Ltd, company no. 17360422.

Phone 07312 132517 · info@rutlanddriveways.co.uk · Mon–Sat 8am–6pm · Google Business Profile: https://share.google/wUltFD4kzvO62EHpd

Areas: Oakham, Uppingham, Stamford, Market Harborough, Corby and Kettering, and the villages of Ketton, Empingham, Cottesmore, Greetham, Langham, Whissendine, Ryhall, Edith Weston, Weldon and Great Bowden, with the rest of Rutland. Dropped kerbs: we hold the NRSWA street works qualification and build crossings in every area we cover.

## 2026 guide prices (all in)

- Resin bound driveways £150–£220 per m² (two-car drive of 40–50m² usually £7,500–£11,000)
- Block paving £120–£170 per m²
- Tarmac £90–£130 per m² on a rebuilt base; plane and re-top £45–£70 per m²
- Stabilised gravel £60–£100 per m²
- Porcelain patios £150–£200 per m²; Indian sandstone £130–£180 per m²
- Full garden transformation £15,000–£35,000; refresh £6,000–£12,000
- Garage conversion £14,000–£19,000 (part conversion from £9,500)
- Single storey extension £2,400–£3,200 per m²
- Enclosed porch £8,500–£14,000; oak-framed porch from £4,500
- Hot tub base from £2,000; swim spa slab £4,000–£6,500; part-sunk from £17,500; fully sunk from £25,000
- Tarmac plane and re-top £45–£70 per m²
- Louvred aluminium pergola supplied and fitted from £4,500 (3m × 4m on a suitable base)
- Composite decking £200–£250 per m², softwood decking £110–£140 per m²
- Closeboard fencing £80–£100 per metre; composite and aluminium slatted from about £240 per metre
- Permeable block paving £140–£210 per m²; channel drains £120–£200 per metre installed
- Glass veranda 4m × 3m £9,000–£14,000
- Outdoor kitchen from about £6,000; fully equipped £8,000–£20,000
- Built-in fire pit £1,200–£2,000; with seating from £3,500
- Automated sliding gates £5,000–£10,000; swing gates £4,000–£8,000
- Bin store fitted from about £1,000
- Garden lighting scheme up to £1,500; full garden £2,000–£6,000+
- Access ramp with handrails up to about £2,500; Disabled Facilities Grant work

## Council rules (checked October 2026)

- Oakham, Uppingham and Rutland villages: highways Rutland County Council, planning Rutland County Council. Dropped kerb: £194 for a Section 184 vehicle access permit (one or two homes); built by an approved contractor with street works accreditation and the right insurance, working under the council's permit. Pre-application advice £210. Building control: Leicestershire Building Control Partnership (LBCP).
- Stamford: highways Lincolnshire County Council, planning South Kesteven District Council. Dropped kerb: £300 if Lincolnshire County Council builds it (the council puts a typical crossing at £2,500–£3,500, tarmac only, 2.75m wide), or £470 if an accredited contractor builds it; built by the county council itself, or an accredited contractor with £10m public liability insurance and NRSWA-qualified operatives, which we can do for you. Pre-application advice £90. Building control: East Midlands Building Consultancy (South Kesteven's building control service).
- Market Harborough: highways Leicestershire County Council, planning Harborough District Council. Dropped kerb: £300 to apply, then either the county council builds it at a quoted price, or an accredited contractor builds it under a £240 permit; built by the county council at a quoted price, or an accredited contractor with £10m public liability insurance and an NRSWA street works card, which we can do for you. Pre-application advice £101. Building control: Leicestershire Building Control Partnership (LBCP).
- Corby and Kettering: highways North Northamptonshire Council, planning North Northamptonshire Council. Dropped kerb: £333 licence and inspection fee; built by a contractor approved by the council, which we can do for you. Pre-application advice £187. Building control: North Northamptonshire Council building control.
- Stamford conservation area (Britain's first, 1967) has an Article 4 direction since December 2018: road-facing hard surfaces, walls, gates, porches and extensions need planning permission.
- 17 Rutland villages have Article 4 directions, including Lyddington, Seaton, Braunston, Langham, Preston and Tinwell.
- National: householder planning application £548, lawful development certificate £274 (from April 2026).
